en: to become crooked; to be bent out of shape

examples.en: The frame was crooked, so I hung it again.
Your hat is crooked, so try putting it on straight.
I had a friend who turned rebellious in puberty.

examples.ko: 아이의 이가 삐뚤어지게 나서 교정을 해요.
examples.en: The child's teeth are coming in crooked, so they are getting braces.
If your posture gets crooked, your back hurts.

examples.ko: 삐뚤어지려고 한 게 아니라 속상했을 뿐이에요.
examples.en: I wasn't trying to act out. I was just upset.

explain: '비뚤어지다'와 같은 말이고, 물건이나 자세가 바르지 않을 때 써요. '마음이 삐뚤어지다, 삐뚤어지게 굴다'처럼 성격이나 태도가 비꼬이고 엇나갈 때도 쓰는 비유예요.

phrases.en: My glasses were crooked, so I straightened them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삐뚤어지다'와 같은 말이고, 조금 더 순한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same word as 삐뚤어지다, with a slightly milder feel.

phrases.en: I straightened the crooked picture frame.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 형태로, 바르지 않게 기운 물건에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun, for things that tilt out of line.

phrases.en: I kept comparing myself and my attitude turned sour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격이나 마음이 비꼬이고 엇나갈 때 쓰는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for a mind or attitude turning twisted and contrary.

explain_en: It is the same word as '비뚤어지다', used when an object or posture is not straight. It is also used figuratively, as in '마음이 삐뚤어지다' and '삐뚤어지게 굴다', for a twisted personality or attitude.

en: to be unsatisfactory; to be disappointing; to be unsatisfying

examples.ko: 이 식당은 음식 맛이 시원찮아서 다시 가고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: The food at this restaurant is disappointing, so I don't want to go again.

examples.ko: 요즘 입맛이 시원찮아서 밥을 반만 먹었어요.
examples.en: My appetite hasn't been great lately, so I only ate half my rice.
I got a disappointing report card, so I'm upset.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 음식 맛이 좀 시원찮아요.
examples.en: The food at that restaurant is a bit underwhelming.
The vacuum cleaner I just bought is really not up to much.
If the answer isn't satisfying, ask again.
You don't look so well today.

explain: '시원치 않다'의 준말이에요. 결과, 반응, 몸 상태가 기대만 못할 때 쓰고 '신통찮다'와 비슷해요. '시원찮은 대답', '입맛이 시원찮다'처럼 나쁜 평가를 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm not feeling great today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시원찮다'의 원래 모양이고 말이나 글에서 둘 다 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The original form of 시원찮다, used in both speech and writing.

phrases.en: I only got an unsatisfying answer to my question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대에 못 미치는 말이나 반응을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for words or reactions that fall short of expectations.

phrases.en: That store's business doesn't look good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 보기에 별로일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something looks poor from the outside.

explain_en: It is the short form of '시원치 않다'. You use it when a result, a reaction or someone's condition falls short of what you hoped, much like '신통찮다'. It always gives a negative judgment, as in '시원찮은 대답' or '입맛이 시원찮다'.

t90.ax: You don't look so well today.

en: to be dark; to be gloomy; to be dimly lit

examples.en: The room was dim, so I turned on the light.
The underground parking lot is gloomy even during the day.
I heard a cat's cry in the dark alley.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 낮에도 하늘이 어두컴컴해요.
examples.en: On rainy days, the sky is dark even in the daytime.
It's dark inside the cave, so bring a flashlight.
Let's head home before it gets dark.

explain: 그냥 '어둡다'보다 컴컴하고 조금 음침한 느낌이 있어요. '어둑하다'는 해 질 무렵처럼 약간 어두울 때 쓰고, '어두컴컴하다'는 그보다 더 깜깜하고 답답한 곳에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I read a book alone in a dim room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 답답하고 어두운 장소에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form describes the noun after it. It fits stuffy, dark places.

phrases.en: It's raining, so it's dim outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금의 상태를 말하는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form, describing how things look right now.

phrases.en: When the clouds came in, the sky became dim.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어둡지 않았다가 점점 어두워지는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a change from not dark to getting dim.

explain_en: Place looks heavily dark and gloomy, like a room with no light. It feels murkier and slightly gloomier than plain '어둡다'. '어둑하다' is for mild darkness, like dusk, while '어두컴컴하다' fits darker, stuffier places.

t90.ax: Let's head home before it gets dark.

examples.en: I look up words I don't know in a Korean dictionary.
I bought a Korean dictionary in paper form.
It's not in the Korean dictionary, but everyone uses it.
I often open the Korean dictionary when doing homework.
I installed a Korean dictionary app on my phone.

examples.ko: 이 낱말 뜻은 국어사전에 이렇게 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The meaning of this word is given like this in the Korean dictionary.

explain: 한국 사람이 한국어 낱말의 뜻을 찾는 사전이에요. 학교에서 '국어'는 한국어 과목을 말하기 때문에 '국어사전'이라고 불러요. 요즘은 종이책보다 인터넷 사전이나 앱으로 많이 찾아요.

phrases.en: If you don't know the meaning, look it up in a Korean dictionary.
phrases.nuance_ko: '찾다'나 '찾아보다'와 함께 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used with 찾다 or 찾아보다.
phrases.en_equiv: look up in a Korean dictionary

phrases.en: I looked up the word in an online Korean dictionary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이책이 아니라 컴퓨터나 앱으로 찾는 사전을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a dictionary on a computer or app, not a paper book.

phrases.en: This word isn't in the Korean dictionary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 말이 정식 낱말인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whether a word is an official entry.

explain_en: Reference book listing Korean words and meanings; everyday tool. This is the dictionary Koreans use to look up the meaning of Korean words. At school, '국어' is the Korean language subject, hence the name. These days people more often search online or in apps than in paper books.

examples.en: I met a friend on the way to school and we walked together.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 오늘 등굣길이 많이 막혔어요.
examples.en: It rained, so the road to school was very congested today.
The morning walk to school is always busy and hectic.

examples.ko: 아이들의 등굣길을 지켜 주는 어르신들이 계세요.
examples.en: There are elders who watch over the children on their way to school.
There was almost an accident at the crosswalk on the way to school.
There is a small bakery on my way to school.

explain: 학교에 가는 길이나 그 시간을 말하고, 반대말은 '하굣길'이에요. '출근길', '퇴근길'과 같은 짝으로 기억하면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: On my way to school, I bought milk at a convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-에'를 붙여 학교 가는 도중에 한 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -에 describes what you did on the way to school.

phrases.en: It started to rain on the way to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등굣길'을 풀어 쓴 말로, 뜻이 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out version of 등굣길 with the same meaning.

phrases.en: On the way home from school, I eat tteokbokki with friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등굣길'의 반대말이에요. 학교에서 집으로 가는 길이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 등굣길: the way home from school.

explain_en: It means the road to school or the time spent going there, and the opposite is '하굣길'. It pairs well with '출근길' and '퇴근길' in your memory.

examples.en: You receive the question sheet when the test starts.
You must not doodle on the question sheet.
We were short of question sheets, so I made copies.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나면 답안지와 문제지도 같이 내요.
examples.en: When the test ends, you hand in the question sheet along with the answer sheet.
The print on this question sheet is too small.
Be sure to check the back of the question sheet too.

explain: 시험에서 문제가 적힌 종이는 문제지, 답을 쓰는 종이는 답안지예요. 연습으로 풀어 보는 종이는 보통 '학습지'라고 해요. 시험 때 주로 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I received the exam paper from the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 시작 때 가장 먼저 하는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The first thing you do when an exam begins.

phrases.en: The exam ended, so the teacher collected the papers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험이 끝난 뒤 종이를 모을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when papers are collected after the exam.

phrases.en: Please check the question sheet and the answer sheet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 적힌 종이와 답을 쓰는 종이를 같이 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the question sheet and answer sheet together.

explain_en: In an exam, the sheet with the questions is 문제지 and the sheet you write answers on is 답안지. A sheet used for practice is usually called 학습지. The word is mainly used around tests.

examples.en: A new method is being tried for the first time.
That experiment was attempted several times.
It is something that has never been tried.
It is planned to be tried next month.
Various approaches are being tried.
Even if it is tried, success is hard.

explain: 새 방법이나 실험을 해 본다는 사실을 말할 때, 해 본 사람을 밝히지 않고 써요. '시도된 적이 없다', '여러 번 시도되다'처럼 자주 써요. 뉴스나 설명하는 글에서 주로 써서 말할 때는 '해 보다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 이런 방법은 한국에서 시도된 적이 없어요.
phrases.en: This method has never been tried in Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 해 보는 일이라고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say something has never been tried before.

phrases.example: 새로운 수업 방식이 여러 학교에서 시도되고 있어요.
phrases.en: A new teaching method is being tried in several schools.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 해 보고 있는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is being tried right now.

phrases.example: 저도 그 방법을 한번 해 봐요.
phrases.en: I'll try that method once too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시도되다'는 글에서 쓰고, 말할 때는 '해 보다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: 시도되다 is for writing; 해 보다 sounds more natural in speech.

explain_en: Used to say that a new method or experiment is being tried, without naming who tries it. Phrases like 'has never been tried' and 'was tried several times' are common. It is mostly for news and explanatory writing; in speech, the plain phrase for 'give it a try' sounds more natural.

en: to apply; to put into effect

examples.en: The teacher applies a new rule.
I applied the grammar I learned to speaking.

examples.ko: 할인은 모든 상품에 적용할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The discount cannot be applied to every item.

examples.ko: 이 방법을 일에 적용해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to try applying this method at work.
I applied the coupon and then paid.
The newly applied system is complicated.

explain: 규칙, 방법, 쿠폰, 이론을 실제 상황에 쓸 때 써요. 영어 apply에는 지원한다는 뜻이 있지만 '적용하다'는 지원서를 내는 뜻이 아니에요. 지원할 때는 '지원하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Please try applying the new method once.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'를 붙여서 한번 시험 삼아 써 본다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 보다' means trying it out to see how it works.

phrases.en: This coupon applies to all products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 쿠폰이 어디에 쓰이는지 말할 때 써요. 내가 쓰면 '적용하다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where a rule or coupon applies. When a person applies it, use '적용하다'.

phrases.en: We apply the same rule to all students.
phrases.nuance_ko: '규칙', '기준'과 같이 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation with words like 'rule' and 'standard'.

explain_en: Put a rule or method into effect on something. Used for putting a rule, method, coupon or theory into real use. Unlike the English word 'apply', it does not mean applying for a job; that uses the separate verb for applying.

dis.h: put a rule or method into effect
gh: adapt learned knowledge for real-life use

p.n: 응용하다 means adapting knowledge, not applying a rule to people, so it does not fit.

t90.ax: The teacher applies a new rule.

examples.en: The teacher graded the exam papers all night.
I'll grade your homework and return it tomorrow.
The computer grades the answers automatically.
Please take a short break while I grade.
Shall we swap and grade each other's?

examples.ko: 채점한 결과를 보니까 점수가 많이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Looking at the graded results, my score went up a lot.

explain: '채점하다'는 시험지나 숙제의 정답과 점수를 매기는 일이에요. 누가 하는지에 따라 '선생님이 채점하다', '스스로 채점하다'처럼 주어가 바뀌어요. 점수를 '받다'는 쪽은 학생이고 '채점하다'는 점수를 주는 쪽이에요.

phrases.en: After the exam, the teacher grades it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '채점하다'와 뜻이 같고, '을/를'을 넣어 말할 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 채점하다, with the object particle added.

phrases.en: When the grading is done, I'll tell you the score.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채점 작업이 다 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the grading work is finished.

phrases.en: Look at the answers and grade it yourself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생이 자기 시험지를 직접 채점할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when students grade their own papers.

explain_en: 채점하다 means checking answers and assigning a score to an exam or homework. The subject changes by who does it, as in 선생님이 채점하다 and 스스로 채점하다. The student is the one who receives a score, and the one who 채점하다 is the one giving it.

examples.en: Today's game has many things worth watching for.
I posted my viewing review of the match on my blog.

examples.ko: 저는 직접 하는 것보다 관전을 더 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like watching games more than playing them myself.
Good spectator manners make it fun for everyone.

examples.ko: 축구 관전 후에 친구들과 치킨을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After watching the soccer match, I ate fried chicken with friends.

examples.ko: 이번 관전으로 선수들 이름을 다 외웠어요.
examples.en: After watching this time, I learned all the players' names.

explain: 경기, 바둑, 대결을 구경할 때 써요. 영화나 공연을 보는 것은 '관람'이라고 해서 쓰는 곳이 달라요. 방송에서는 '관전 포인트'라는 말이 자주 들려요.

phrases.example: 주말에 경기 관전을 하러 갈 거예요.
phrases.en: I'm going to watch a game this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관전' 앞에 '경기'를 붙여 무엇을 구경하는지 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'game' in front makes clear what is being watched.

phrases.en: Please follow good spectator manners at the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기를 볼 때 지켜야 하는 예의를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the etiquette you should keep while watching a match.

phrases.example: 결승전의 관전 포인트는 두 선수의 속도예요.
phrases.en: The key thing to watch in the final is the two players' speed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기에서 특히 눈여겨볼 점을 말할 때 방송에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used on broadcasts for what to pay special attention to in a match.

explain_en: Watching a sports match or game, often as a spectator. Use it for watching a game, a Go match, or a contest. Watching a movie or a performance is 관람, so the two are used in different places. On TV you often hear the phrase 관전 포인트 (what to watch for).

examples.en: A soldier blows the bugle every morning.
When the bugle sounds, everyone gathers.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 나팔처럼 큰 소리로 노래했어요.
examples.en: That child sang as loudly as a trumpet.
A morning glory blooms in the morning and wilts by day.
I bought pants with a flared, trumpet-shaped hem.

examples.ko: 행진할 때 나팔과 북이 같이 울렸어요.
examples.en: During the parade, trumpets and drums sounded together.

explain: 입으로 부는 금속 악기를 말하고 '나팔을 불다'라고 해요. 모양이 닮은 것에 붙여 '나팔꽃', '나팔바지'라고 해요. 오케스트라 악기를 정확히 말할 때는 '트럼펫'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My older brother played the bugle at a school event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기를 연주할 때는 '불다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 불다 when playing this instrument.

phrases.en: The morning glories bloomed wide this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃 모양이 나팔을 닮아서 붙은 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The flower is named for its trumpet-like shape.

phrases.en: I heard my father wore bell-bottoms when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아래가 나팔처럼 넓게 퍼진 바지예요.
phrases.nuance_en: These are pants that flare wide at the bottom like a horn.

explain_en: Simple horn blown at marches or signals; also flared shape. It means a brass instrument blown by mouth, and the verb phrase is '나팔을 불다'. It is attached to things shaped similarly, as in '나팔꽃' (morning glory) and '나팔바지' (flared pants). For the exact orchestral instrument, people say '트럼펫'.

t90.ax: That child sang as loudly as a trumpet.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 올해 도루를 서른 개나 했어요.
examples.en: That player had thirty stolen bases this year.
The steal succeeded and the team moved ahead.

examples.ko: 도루 성공률이 높은 선수가 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: Players with a high steal success rate are popular.
The steal failed and the crowd sighed.
The player named stolen-base leader gave an interview.
As steal attempts grew, the games got faster.

explain: 야구 중계에서는 '도루 성공', '도루 실패', '도루왕'처럼 기록을 말할 때 많이 나와요. '득점', '타점'과 함께 기록 말로 알아 두면 좋아요. 야구를 모르는 사람에게는 잘 쓰지 않는 말이에요.

phrases.en: That player succeeded in stealing a base.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구 중계에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in baseball broadcasts.
phrases.en_equiv: to succeed in stealing a base

phrases.en: He failed to steal the base and was out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성공'의 반대로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 성공 in this pairing.
phrases.en_equiv: to fail to steal a base

phrases.en: Last year's stolen base leader is that player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해에 도루를 가장 많이 한 선수를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for the player with the most steals in a season.

explain_en: In baseball broadcasts it appears when recording stats, as in '도루 성공', '도루 실패' and '도루왕'. It is good to learn it together with '득점' and '타점'. It is not a word used with people who don't follow baseball.

examples.en: At the ski resort I rode the lift up to the top.
The lift suddenly stopped and I was a little scared.

examples.ko: 리프트 표는 매표소에서 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy lift tickets at the ticket office.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 리프트 운행이 중단됐어요.
examples.en: The lift stopped running because of the heavy snow.
In winter the line in front of the lift is long.
The view looking down from the lift was really beautiful.

explain: 한국에서 '리프트'는 주로 스키장이나 관광지의 의자 리프트를 가리켜요. 건물 안에서 타는 것은 '엘리베이터'라고 하고 '리프트'라고 하지 않아요. 휠체어용 승강 장치도 '휠체어 리프트'라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 스키 리프트 앞에 사람들이 줄을 섰어요.
phrases.en: People lined up in front of the ski lift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스키장에서 올라갈 때 타는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ride used to go up at a ski resort.

phrases.en: There is a wheelchair lift at the subway station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휠체어를 위로 옮겨 주는 장치예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A device that moves a wheelchair up or down.

phrases.en: Be careful when you get off the lift.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타다'와 짝이 되는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of '타다' (to ride).

explain_en: In Korea, '리프트' mostly means a chair lift at ski resorts or tourist sites. The thing you ride inside buildings is an '엘리베이터', not a '리프트'. A wheelchair platform lift is '휠체어 리프트'.
